in_arabic.name: معاديني
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم معاديني مشتق من الجذر العربي 'عاد' الذي يحمل معاني العودة والإعادة. يعني الاسم الشخص الذي يُعاد إلى الأصل أو المرجع الذي يُرجع إليه. في السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن يشير إلى الشخص الذي يعود إلى الله أو يعيد النظر في أصوله الدينية. اسم معاديني يوحي بالعمق الروحي والتواصل مع الجذور.

in_urdu.name: معادینی
in_urdu.meaning: اصل کی طرف لوٹنے والا، مرجع
in_urdu.long_meaning: معادینی نام عربی جڑ 'عاد' سے نکلا ہے، جس کے معنی واپسی یا دوبارہ آنے کے ہیں۔ یہ نام اس شخص کے لیے استعمال ہوتا ہے جو اپنے اصل یا مرجع کی طرف لوٹتا ہے۔ اسلامی سیاق و سباق میں، یہ نام اس شخص کی نشاندہی کر سکتا ہے جو اللہ کی طرف لوٹتا ہے یا اپنی مذہبی جڑوں پر غور کرتا ہے۔ معادینی نام روحانی گہرائی اور جڑوں سے منسلک ہونے کا احساس دلاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: मुआदिनी
in_hindi.meaning: मूल की ओर लौटने वाला, संदर्भ
in_hindi.long_meaning: मुआदिनी नाम अरबी मूल 'عاد' से निकला है, जिसका अर्थ है वापसी या पुनः आगमन। यह नाम उस व्यक्ति के लिए प्रयोग किया जाता है जो अपने मूल या संदर्भ की ओर लौटता है। इस्लामी संदर्भ में, यह नाम उस व्यक्ति को इंगित कर सकता है जो अल्लाह की ओर लौटता है या अपनी धार्मिक जड़ों पर विचार करता है। मुआदिनी नाम आध्यात्मिक गहराई और जड़ों से जुड़ने की भावना को दर्शाता है।

in_pashto.name: معاديني
in_pashto.meaning: د اصلي ته د راستنېدونکی، حوالې
in_pashto.long_meaning: معاديني نوم د عربي ريښې 'عاد' څخه اخستل شوی دی، کوم چې د بېرته ستنېدلو يا بيا راتلو معنی لري. دا نوم د هغه چا لپاره کارول کيږي چي خپل اصلي يا حوالې ته بېرته ستنیږي. په اسلامي سياق کې، دا نوم د هغه چا اشاره کولی شي چي الله ته بېرته ستنیږي يا خپل مذهبي ريښو ته پام کوي. معاديني نوم روحاني يو ډولتيا او ريښو سره نښلول احساس ورکوي.

in_english.name: Muaddini
in_english.meaning: One who returns to the origin or reference
in_english.long_meaning: The name Muaddini is derived from the Arabic root 'عاد' (ʿād), which carries meanings related to return or coming back. It refers to someone who returns to their origin or serves as a reference point. In an Islamic context, the name may signify a person who turns back to God or reflects on their religious roots. Muaddini suggests spiritual depth and a connection to one's roots, emphasizing a return to fundamental principles or a primary source.

data.cultural_impact: The title "Muaddini" holds significant cultural importance in the Islamic world as it is associated with the propagation of Islamic teachings and the enhancement and preservation of Islamic knowledge. This title has been esteemed in the Islamic community for centuries, with many notable scholars and teachers carrying this title. A Muaddini is not only seen as an educator but also as a guide and a role model for others, spreading the message of Islam and inspiring others to seek knowledge and righteousness.
data.spiritual_significance: The title "Muaddini" carries immense spiritual significance for Muslims as it represents the act of inviting others to the path of Allah, and the dedication to teaching and sharing the knowledge of Islam. It is a reminder of the importance of spreading awareness of the teachings of Islam and striving to guide others towards a deeper understanding and connection with Allah. The title also symbolizes the desire to continuously seek knowledge and further our relationship with God, inspiring a commitment to lifelong learning and spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: Muaddib al-Arab, or Imam al-Haramain, was a prominent scholar of the ninth century AH. He is best known for his role as the chief qadi (judge) of Cairo during the Ayyubid period. Muaddib al-Arab played a crucial role in the development and codification of the Hanafi school of Islamic jurisprudence.

Muaddib al-Sanussi was a prominent Sufi scholar and founder of the Sanusiyya order in the late 18th century AH (early 20th century AD). He is known for his role in the resistance against Italian colonization of Libya and for his importance in the development of the Sanusiyya Sufi order.

modern_usage.modern_context: The term 'Muaddini' originated from the Islamic tradition, where Muaddin was the official caller to prayer in a mosque. In modern times, this term has evolved to represent individuals and organizations dedicated to religious education, community engagement, and digital learning in Islamic contexts. These efforts can be seen across various platforms, including mobile applications, social media, and e-learning websites. Muaddini organizations and apps provide a range of services, from Quranic education and prayer reminders to community forums and virtual mosques. The trend towards digital learning and community engagement is particularly strong among younger Muslims, who are increasingly turning to technology to access religious content and connect with others. As a result, the role of Muaddini in the digital age is evolving to include not only the traditional functions of religious education and community organization, but also the creation and dissemination of digital religious content and the use of technology to facilitate religious experiences and connections.
